Status.note: Evergy's first quarter 2025 earnings presentation from May 2025 lists a delayed retirement and conversion to natural gas for Jeffrey unit 2. Sierra Club comments filed in Missouri in May 2025 say the 2025 plan stops coal burning at unit 2 in 2030 with a gas conversion. The EIA-860M table for August 2026 lists generator 2 as an operating coal unit built in 1980. That row is the coal unit, which GEM carries as the earlier timepoint. So the gas conversion is still only planned and the status stays announced. Both sources describe the same Evergy plan, so this counts as one source.

Start year.note: The Sierra Club table in its May 2025 comments to the Missouri Public Service Commission shows Jeffrey 2 as a gas conversion in 2030 in Evergy's 2025 plan update. The table gives the year coal burning stops, not the first day on gas, so the value is only implied.

Planned retire.note: The same table shows Jeffrey 2 with a 2039 retirement date in Evergy's 2025 plan update, after the 2030 gas conversion. So the 2039 date still holds. The EIA-860M table for August 2026 lists 2039 for generator 1 and nothing for generator 2, so it does not confirm it.

Conversion/replacement?.note: Evergy's first quarter 2025 earnings presentation calls it a delayed retirement and conversion to natural gas for Jeffrey unit 2. The Sierra Club comments say the same. So the value conversion is correct.

Latest Activity.note: The newest report I found that names the Jeffrey unit 2 gas conversion is the Sierra Club comments dated May 7, 2025. Evergy's presentation is also from May 2025. Evergy's June 2026 plan update slides do not mention Jeffrey. So the project looks quiet for more than a year.

Status Detail.value: In May 2025, Evergy's 2025 plan update kept a gas conversion of Jeffrey unit 2 in 2030 with retirement in 2039. Evergy's June 2026 plan update slides do not name Jeffrey.
Status Detail.note: New sentence for the top of the box. The box is blank today. It is based on the May 2025 earnings presentation and the Sierra Club comments.

units.notes: No document gives a turbine model or a capacity for the converted gas unit. The 720 MW in GEM is the coal unit nameplate in the EIA-860M table for August 2026. The coal unit is still operating, so the gas conversion has not happened.

Owner(s).value: Evergy Kansas Central Inc [92%]; Evergy Missouri West Inc [8%]
Owner(s).note: Evergy's 2024 annual report says Evergy Kansas Central owns 92 percent of Jeffrey Energy Center and that Evergy Missouri West owns 8 percent. GEM splits the 92 percent into 72 percent Kansas Central and 20 percent Kansas South. The report does not show that split. Evergy Kansas South is the former Kansas Gas and Electric, so the 20 percent may sit inside the 92 percent. A reviewer should decide whether to keep the split.

qa.recommendation: I could not find the exact month the unit reached announced status. The earliest documents I found are Evergy's June 2023 plan update, which added a placeholder to retire Jeffrey unit 2 in 2030, and the May 2025 plan update, which lists a gas conversion in 2030. The 2025 plan update is the first one I found that calls it a conversion to gas. A reviewer may use 2025.

qa.recommendation: The EIA-860M table for August 2026 lists a planned retirement of 2039 for Jeffrey generator 1, none for generator 2 and 2030 for generator 3. The Sierra Club table lists 2039 for generator 1 and 2030 for generator 3 in the 2025 plan update too. GEM's 2039 for unit 2 follows the Sierra Club table for the gas unit.
qa.note: EIA and the plan agree on units 1 and 3 and differ only in leaving unit 2 blank.

qa.recommendation: The 2025 plan update chart for Kansas Central shows coal retirements of 674 MW in 2031 and 855 MW in 2033 without naming plants. The 2026 plan update slide shows no retirements. I could not tie any Evergy plan slide to a Jeffrey retirement or conversion date, so I used the Sierra Club table, which reads Evergy's full plan filing.
